calls.head: Who drives the play: the Panthers
calls.body: At 5-on-5, the Panthers have been around the middle of the league at getting more of the chances than they give up, and the Blackhawks one of the worst. The ice should tilt the Panthers’ way, even if goaltending and bounces have the final say on the score.

calls.body: On physicality, Florida is the league’s best, but Chicago is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Expect most of the big hits to come from the Panthers.

surprises.head: Florida’s power play was at its best
surprises.body: Florida has one of the league’s most dangerous power plays. Even by those standards, this was a big night: 22.3 expected goals per 60 on the power play, against their usual 8.8 (about 8.4 against Chicago) and a league average of 7.7. A team strays this far about once every 125 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

story.head: Four points for Vilmanis as the Panthers beat the Blackhawks
paras: Sandis Vilmanis opened the scoring for the Panthers early in the first, and Carter Verhaeghe pushed the lead to 2-0 on the power play midway through the period. Seth Jones stretched the lead to 3-0 midway through the second. Roman Kantserov got the Blackhawks on the board three and a half minutes later. It was a busy third period. Frank Nazar cut Florida’s lead to 3-2 shorthanded midway through the period. Vilmanis scored his second of the night a minute and a half later to make it 4-2 for the Cats, and that one stood up as the winner. Nazar scored again with just under four minutes left to pull the Blackhawks within one, and Sam Reinhart shut the door with an empty-netter with a minute and a half left. Reinhart finished with a goal and two assists, and Vilmanis added two assists for a four-point night.

The Panthers drove the play, outshooting the Blackhawks 30-20, and the scoreboard caught up. Jacob Markström made 17 saves for the Panthers, and Spencer Knight stopped 25 of 29 at the other end. The Panthers improved to 9-5-2, fifth in the Atlantic, while the Blackhawks dropped to 4-11-1, still last in the Central.
